summary: Ngawang Jinpa works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling. He taught Samdhong Rinpoche and Kevin A. Vose.

Ngawang Jorden specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Sakya College and served as director at the International Buddhist Academy around 2009. He taught Christian Bernert and Constance E. Kassor.

Ngawang Samten is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Lati Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Tsering, Jampa Yeshe, and Konchok Tsering. He directed the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~2001–2021) and held posts at Smith College (2004), Hampshire, Amherst College, and the University of Tasmania.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet is a Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University (~2008–2012) under doctoral supervisor Inder Mohan Singh, and studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Punjabi University (~2009–2013) under the doctoral supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann.
Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~2005–2009) under doctoral supervisors Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi in 1993, where he was supervised for his MA by K. T. S. Sarao.

Nianzu Huang worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and with Nordan Hutuktu, Gangkar Rinpoche, Hsu Yun, Lianju Xia, and Jiaqi Wang. He was head at Central People's Broadcasting Station and a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.
Nichidatsu Fujii was active in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Rissho University, founded Nipponzan Myohoji, and taught Gyoryo Maruyama.

Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a professor at the University of Ceylon (~1962–1978) and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1978–1984), and he taught David J. Kalupahana and Dhammanandā.

Nicholas J. Allen specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Rugby School and the University of Oxford. He held posts at SOAS, Durham University, Wolfson College, Oxford, and served as Lecturer in the Social Anthropology of South Asia at Oxford (~1976–2001).

Nicholas Poppe was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1916–1921), where he later served as Professor of Mongolian (~1925–1941), alongside posts at academic institutes in Russia and the University of Washington (~1949–1968).
Nicholas Ribush works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1975, he studied under traditional teachers Thubten Yeshe and Thubten Zopa Rinpoche.

Nicholas Roerich worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Higher Art School at the Imperial Academy of Arts (~1893–1897) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1893–1898).
Nicholas Sims-Williams is a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Borden Grammar School (~1960–1967) and held a post at SOAS University of London (~1976–2014).
Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Stanford University (~2009–2015) and held a post as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo.

Nicholson T. Collier is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD at the University of Chicago (~1991–1998) under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths and committee member David Tracy.

Nicola Bajetta is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. at the University of Hamburg (~2017–2020), where he studied with teacher Fabian Sanders and committee member Harunaga Isaacson.

Nicola Di Cosmo works in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Indiana State University and Indiana University. He held positions at Cambridge, Harvard, the University of Canterbury, and the Institute for Advanced Study.
Nicolas Morrissey specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Gregory Schopen (~2003–2009) and held a post at the University of Georgia around 2011.
